title: The Decision Value of Perception Compute
abstract: arXiv:2609.35910v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adaptive perception spends extra computation on inputs where perception is expected to improve. When perception feeds a downstream decision system, a better perception output need not produce a better decision. We define the decision value of perception compute as the change in downstream loss from escalating an input from a cheap to an expensive perception mode. Because this value can be negative, the allocation of perception compute should be judged against a budget-constrained decision oracle, with uniform full-fidelity inference as a baseline rather than an upper bound. We introduce DEEP (Decision Evaluation for Escalated Perception), a benchmark that scores pre-escalation allocators against this oracle under selection, latency and energy budgets, charging each allocator for its own computation. With deployed monocular geometry on KITTI and nuScenes, we find that 34--54% of the escalations that change downstream loss make it worse; h

translated_title: 感知计算对决策的价值
translated_abstract: 自适应感知会在预期感知性能能够提升的输入上花费额外的计算。然而，当感知结果作为下游决策系统的输入时，更好的感知输出并不一定带来更好的决策。我们将感知计算的决策价值定义为：将某个输入从廉价的感知模式升级到昂贵的感知模式时，下游损失所产生的变化。由于这一价值可能为负，感知计算的分配应当以一个受预算约束的决策预言机（oracle）作为评判标准，而统一的全精度推理只应作为基线而非性能上限。我们提出了DEEP（Decision Evaluation for Escalated Perception，升级感知的决策评估）基准，该基准在选择、延迟和能量预算下，将升级前的分配器与该预言机进行对比评分，并向每个分配器收取其自身计算的开销。在KITTI和nuScenes数据集上使用已部署的单目几何模型，我们发现34%至54%的改变了下游损失的升级反而使损失变得更糟……
tldr: 该论文定义了感知计算升级对下游决策的真实价值，并提出DEEP基准来在多种预算约束下评估感知资源分配策略，发现KITTI和nuScenes上34%-54%改变了下游损失的感知升级反而使决策表现变差，说明感知计算分配应以预算约束的决策oracle为评判标准，而非盲目追求更高感知精度。
en_tdlr: The paper defines the decision value of perception compute and introduces DEEP, a benchmark evaluating pre-escalation allocators against a budget-constrained decision oracle, revealing that on KITTI and nuScenes 34-54% of escalations that change downstream loss actually make decisions worse.
